messages:
Taylor: Hey team — trying to run the runtime unit tests in the dev container and they all report no GPU found. Host has A100s. Inside container: torch.cuda.is_available() -> False, and `nvidia-smi` exits: command not found. Anyone seen this on a dev box?

Morgan: quick checklist: 1) are you running the container with --gpus all or docker runtime? 2) nvidia-container-toolkit installed on host? 3) host drivers >= container CUDA version?

Taylor: I'm using `docker run -it --rm -v $(pwd):/src runtime-dev:latest bash` and then running pytest. I didn't add `--gpus`. Oops. Tried adding `--gpus all` and now `nvidia-smi` shows devices. But pytest still says no CUDA devices inside the test environment (our test uses a small C++ extension that loads libcudart). Error: ImportError: libcudart.so.11.0: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

Janet: ok that sounds like a CUDA runtime library mismatch. The container image is built against 11.0 but host driver provides newer runtime. In container you need libcudart present or set LD_LIBRARY_PATH to host libs via `--volume /usr/local/cuda/lib64...` but prefer using nvidia/cuda base image matching runtime. Try: `docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi`

Taylor: ran that, `nvidia-smi` returns GPU list. But our runtime-dev image is custom (we add some debug tooling). How do folks usually make sure the libs resolve?

Lee: two options: (1) Use NVIDIA's runtime base image as the FROM and install extra deps there (recommended), or (2) bind-mount host driver libs into container (hacky). Example bind mount:

```
docker run --gpus all --rm \
  -v /usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64:/usr/local/cuda/lib64:ro \
  --cap-add SYS_ADMIN runtime-dev:latest bash
```

Also ensure `/etc/nvidia-container-runtime/config.toml` on host has no blacklist of devices.

infra-bot: [node-driver-check] Node gpu-node-42 has driver 525.85.12; container CUDA compatibility OK. No infra action required.

Morgan: also check if pytest spawns a separate lightweight container or uses docker-in-docker in CI — those can miss `--gpus` flags. For local, confirm the process inside container can run `ldconfig -p | grep libcudart` and `python -c \"import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL('libcudart.so')\"`

Taylor: ran `ldconfig -p | grep libcudart` -> empty. So libcudart isn't in container. I'll rebuild FROM `nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime` and repro.

Janet: one more gotcha: ensure the image's `/usr/local/cuda` symlink points to correct cuda dir. We had a flake where `/usr/local/cuda -> cuda-10.2` and tests linked to 11 libs.

Taylor: fixed by switching base image. Tests now see GPUs and pass. Thanks! :tada:

Morgan: nice — add short note to onboarding doc about using `--gpus` and base images. :memo:

Taylor: will do, adding a small snippet to dev-setup.md
